Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — Both reporter-annotated annoyances on the webCG article page reproduce on the locked baseline:⁠ a self-promo premium banner and a "webCGの最新情報を受け取る" subscribe block with a push-notification button. I propose the domain-scoped hide of that subscribe/push block (webcg.net#⁠#⁠.social-btn-2024), which apply_rule verified as resolving the symptom with page integrity intact; the premium banner is reported separately because only one rule may be submitted. ## Rule `webcg.net##.social-btn-2024` ## Policy rationale The reported elements are a site subscription/push-notification prompt and a self-promo banner, i.e. Annoyances in-page subscription elements - they are not the site's first-party advertising of third-party goods, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall, so no run-instruction closing rule applies. The AdGuard filter policy's AdGuard Other Annoyances / Popups scope covers in-page subscription and self-promotion elements, so a domain-scoped cosmetic rule is within policy. The element is served in the page HTML with no distinct request behind it, so element hiding (#⁠#⁠) - not a network rule - is the appropriate and least invasive fix. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a5e57a2974a94177ab37e2bd51acf2c2e3111a88/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — Reporter target:⁠ circled InMobi Choice consent dialog ("We value your privacy" / MORE OPTIONS · DISAGREE · AGREE) over a dimmed Satoshi→EUR converter page. Network log (artifact:⁠har:⁠a5103adf-0371-4c67-b9a2-283b68163a75):⁠ cmp.inmobi.com/choice/f7v-JN5FmsdpM/awebanalysis.com/choice.js?tag_version=V3 (script, 200), cmp.inmobi.com/tcfv2/cmp2.js?referer=awebanalysis.com (script, 200), cmp.inmobi.com/geoip (xhr, 200), cmp.inmobi.com/GVL-v3/vendor-list-trimmed-v1.json (xhr, 200) — a third-party vendor host; __tcfapiLocator frame present, window.__tcfapi answers getTCData. get_applied_rules showed no published rule acting on cmp.inmobi.com. search_rules:⁠ no rule for awebanalysis.com; the vendor's shared rule ||cmp.inmobi.com^$domain=… sits at AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt:⁠114 without this domain. apply_rule:⁠ ||cmp.inmobi.com^$domain=awebanalysis.com verified by network verification (blockedHost cmp.inmobi.com; phase A 4 allowed/0 blocked, phase C 0 allowed/1 blocked; no new third-party hosts), failedCandidateChecks empty, remainingInstances empty, observedDamage empty, structure facts identical before/after (document height 4110 both, same headings, breadcrumbs, media and controls). Complete full-page vision of the proxied session (coverageComplete true, 7/7 tiles, evidenceArtifact full-page-visual-inventory-a4733f0e7417b998) reports the reporter's dialog absent in this environment, matching the CMP's own gdprApplies:⁠false answer; no geographic proxy backend exists to trigger the region-gated banner, so visitor-region gating remains an unverified hypothesis. ## Rule `||cmp.inmobi.com^$domain=awebanalysis.com` ## Policy rationale The report is a third-party CMP cookie notice, which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter is explicitly designed to block; the policy's no-rule rules (first-party ads, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls, scam pages) do not apply. The page shows only a consent dialog over already loaded content, not an anti-adblock detector, so no anti-adblock gate is involved. The fix fits the existing shared ||cmp.inmobi.com^$domain=… network family, so the reported domain may be added to it (or carried as the same rule scoped to the domain). ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a5e57a2974a94177ab37e2bd51acf2c2e3111a88/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 114](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a5e57a2974a94177ab37e2bd51acf2c2e3111a88/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L114). ## Missing information - Run instruction lacks guidance for region-gated consent banners that cannot be reproduced: The reported symptom is an InMobi Choice CMP cookie dialog. The run instruction routes this report to network-level filtering and asks for live reproduction, but no geographic proxy backend is available:⁠ in the locked adguard_cli session the CMP loads and answers window.__tcfapi('getTCData') with gdprApplies:⁠false, so it renders no banner and the reporter's dialog can never be observed here. The instruction does not state whether a candidate that the network verification proves (CMP host blocked on the reported domain, page structure unchanged) counts as "fully validated" when the visual symptom itself could not be reproduced because of visitor-region gating. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

Fallback — The page refused to load in the run browser:⁠ main document returned HTTP 403

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — coincodex.com still serves three third-party sponsored banners (two BC.GAME CPA iframes and a Kraken affiliate bar) through its own EDGE ad config despite the baseline filters; a content-anchored element-hiding rule is proposed for review, but it could not be validated because every reporter-profile session was blocked by an HTTP 403 "Just a moment..." page and the browser attempt budget for the reported URL was exhausted.

## Candidate for review

`coincodex.com##app-mobile-b-position, .s-sq:has(a[rel~="sponsored"]), div:has(> a[href^="https://www.coincodex.com/go/"][rel~="sponsored"])`

BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: No apply_rule experiment could run:⁠ the reported URL returned HTTP 403 'Just a moment...' in the control session and in both reporter-profile (reported_on_current) sessions, and open_page then reported technical_attempt_budget_exhausted (attempt 3/3), so the candidate was never A/B verified and no vision verdict exists. The only session that loaded the page (mobile viewport, defaults_plus_required, imports not the reporter profile) showed the three sponsored creatives and confirmed the selectors match there, but a non-reporter-profile session cannot verify a rule. Single ad-hide rule combining two ad-position containers and one sponsored /go/ wrapper was chosen over blocking ||coincodex.com/*/cpa-bcgame/ because the EDGE creative path segment (823kfxez4m) is server-assigned and the network block would leave empty iframes plus the Kraken bar untouched; a human should confirm it on the reporter's desktop layout.

## Missing information

- No guidance for verifying a candidate when only the reporter profile is blocked: The run instruction's adguard_cli route says to launch evidence sessions with extension:⁠"none" because the proxy filters, but the host refused settings on such a control session and the control's navigation to the reported URL returned HTTP 403 ("Just a moment...", __cf_chl_rt_tk). The reporter-profile session (reported_on_current) also got 403 twice on desktop; only a materially different profile (mobile viewport, consent accept, UTC) loaded the page — and that session used defaults_plus_required, not the reporter import. The run instruction states only a reported_on_current session may verify a rule, and the open_page budget then exhausted (3/3) before a reporter-profile session could load the target. Missing:⁠ how to verify a candidate when the reported URL is reachable only in a different profile, or whether the imported reporter settings (settingsVerified=false in every launch) are applied at all.

A domain-scoped `.st-sns-singular` rule hid the element with page integrity intact but the vision review still saw the residual band (the wrapper's own margin), so the broader `.st-sns-top, .sns.st-sns-singular` candidate is carried for review because the extension environment stopped completing validation phases (phase_proof_unavailable).

Not verified: The extension environment stopped completing validation:⁠ apply_rule answered environment_capability_limited (code phase_proof_unavailable, "The controlled browser observation did not complete") and kept refusing the unchanged limitation even after a fresh launch with identical settings, so this candidate has no phase A/B/C evidence. The narrower variant kamen-rider.info#⁠#⁠.st-sns-singular did run one experiment (adElementStatus .st-sns-singular visible-⁠>hidden, pageIntegrity intact, observedDamage empty) but its vision review reported symptom not_resolved with adLayoutResidue present and one remaining instance; the measured cause is that hiding the bar leaves .st-sns-top's own 20px margin-bottom in place, which is why this candidate also covers .st-sns-top. comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"6c0831978e2a734a77e1da9bae2e54f5f2e115a6d4760cf4c89b9c782154b4c3"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

rothed-db.com forces an ad-monetised Move2Link shortlink (or paid Premium) before any download; the notice is shown to every visitor, not by ad-blocker detection, and the page's own Adsterra script is already blocked by an existing Base-filter rule. This is the site's content-access measure, which the repository policy excludes, so no rule is proposed and closing is recommended.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction policy, 'Paywalls:⁠ no rule; recommend closing' — the download content on rothed-db.com is reachable only through ad-monetised Move2Link shortlinks or a paid Premium membership, i.e. a content-access measure. Filter policy (KnowledgeBase filter-policy.md), 'Limitations and exceptions':⁠ 'Content access measures like paywalls are not blocked by Ad blocking filters.' Run instruction policy, 'The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing', and the policy document's 'The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked. However, it should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules' — the page's own Adsterra ad slot is already handled by the existing generic Base-filter regex, so nothing remains to block. Not an anti-adblock case:⁠ the page contains no ad-blocker detection script and shows the same notice to every visitor, so the anti-adblock clauses (German wall / detector script requirement) do not apply. Hiding the first-party notice would not fix the complaint — it would only delete the user's explanation of the ad/shortlink flow while the ad requirement on Move2Link remains — and blocking move2link.co would break the site's downloads.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/44454302438

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — ominho.pt article pages leave empty "Publicidade" ad slots:⁠ a 268px Google Ad Manager slot mid-article and an AdSense slot band above the "O MINHO / LUSA" card, both showing only reserved blank space once gpt.js is blocked. The rule ominho.pt#⁠#⁠.ominho-ad, .cs-custom-content-pagination-after:⁠has(⁠> center ⁠> .ominho-ad) passed apply_rule verification with the symptom resolved, no remaining instances and page integrity intact. ## Rule `ominho.pt##.ominho-ad, .cs-custom-content-pagination-after:has(> center > .ominho-ad)` ## Policy rationale No filter-policy rule closes this report:⁠ the slots are third-party Google Ad Manager/AdSense placeholders left empty by base filtering, not the site's own advertising, not a paywall and not a German anti-adblock wall. The empty PUBLICIDADE slots occupy large blank areas that stand out against the page, which falls inside the ad-blocking filters' stated purpose ('ads leftovers that occupy large spaces'). ## Place in the list [SpanishFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/dacf7ec53a5326bea81492846b1ab39ecf47cd04/SpanishFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 54](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/dacf7ec53a5326bea81492846b1ab39ecf47cd04/SpanishFilter/sections/specific.txt#L54). ## Screenshots

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://www.mobiel.de/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.mobiel.de%2F) ### Comment > MoBiel is the public transport company of the city Bielefeld. The name is a play on words (Mobility for Bielefeld). The domain is blocked when typosquatting protection is enabled in AdguardDNS. This is not a new company or domain. I wonder how this got on the typosquatting protection list. This is a new issue. Does anyone check whether the affected domains are used deceptively? Even without knowing anything about the company, 30 seconds of investigation or even an automated check against domain registry information and Wikipedia would show that this a reputable, legitimate domain. > > This is not my first complaint the regarding typosquatting protection. Maybe it is better to turn it off, if no reasonable effort is put into assembly of this list. AI slop? ### Screenshots

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported niconico ad chain (preroll video ad in the player and the empty 300x250 sidebar ad card) is already blocked under the reporter's own filter selection:⁠ the unfiltered control shows both, while the reporter-settings prepared session leaves the video-ad container empty, creates no ad-slot iframes at all and blocks ads.nicovideo.jp with existing rules. Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — intercelestial.com shows an English anti-adblock gate ("AdBlock Detected — please disable it") over a dimmed page with html/body scroll-locked; it appears only when filtering blocks the site's first-party ad-unit requests and is painted from a per-load random custom element in a closed shadow root, so no cosmetic selector reaches it. Blocking the ad loader it comes from with ||intercelestial.com/u63f2e02f414/ was verified:⁠ gate gone, page intact, no residue. ## Rule `||intercelestial.com/u63f2e02f414/` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale Run instruction, filter policy:⁠ this is not a German site's anti-adblock wall (English page, English gate text), so that closure rule does not apply. Run instruction:⁠ 'Any other anti-adblock wall:⁠ write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script' — satisfied:⁠ the filtered session's HAR (artifact:⁠har:⁠7131391b-5023-4835-8d30-80b5f8d31a94) captures the third-party anti-adblock host antiadblockcore.com and the first-party ad-unit scripts that request the blockable bait/twin resource pairs and create the randomized gate element. The report is not a request to unblock the site's own advertising and not a paywall report; the fix stops the loader that renders the gate. Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported Facebook outbound-link page (l.facebook.com/l.php -⁠> facebook.com/flx/warn/) is behind a Facebook sign-in wall for this runner in all three bounded attempts, so the reported "tab closes" behaviour could neither be reproduced nor shown absent. With the reporter's exact filter set the engine applied no network rule to that navigation (blockedCount 0, identical chain without any extension) and no repository rule targets l.facebook.com or /flx/warn, so no exception rule could be evidence-backed; the report is left for a maintainer.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — gazetawroclawska.pl shows an Admiral anti-adblock wall ("Pomóż Nam Działać" / "WYŁĄCZ ADBLOCKA", "POWERED BY Admiral") that covers the article and locks scrolling; the wall's loader is the third-party host agonyshark.com, captured in the network log. One network rule, ||agonyshark.com^$domain=gazetawroclawska.pl, was verified in the reporter's MV3 extension session:⁠ the wall is gone, the article is readable and page integrity is intact. ## Rule `||agonyshark.com^$domain=gazetawroclawska.pl` Leftover layout: the page still reserves space where the advertising was. A network rule cannot collapse it; add a cosmetic rule if the gap matters. ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The wall aggressively insists on disabling the ad blocker (single button 'WYŁĄCZ ADBLOCKA', no close option) and effectively prevents using the site:⁠ it covers the article and sets html/body overflow hidden, per the filter policy's condition for blocking anti-adblock walls. The run instruction's evidence gate for a non-German anti-adblock wall is met:⁠ the captured requests show the detector/vendor script from third-party host agonyshark.com. The report is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not a German-language anti-adblock wall, so none of the close rules applies. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/antiadblock.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/73d20011b73ca76479d38ed781115e6bf362e354/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/antiadblock.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

issue.title: Instagram using generated tracking parameters?

labels.name: A: In progress
labels.description: Work on the issue is in progress

issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

I noticed recently that I've been seeing Instagram links from friends where there's a clear tracking parameter, but instead of the usual `igshid`, `igsh`, or `igsi` name, the parameter has some random-looking four character name. In the past couple days alone I've seen `psln`, `srtk`, and `exln`. Earlier I've also observed `stkn` and `vrfl`. The value for each is always 12-13 bytes encoded as base64.

I didn't see these parameters in the [specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/master/TrackParamFilter/sections/specific.txt) list or anyone else reporting this phenomenon, so I wanted to give a head up that they may be encoding/randomizing their tracking parameters. Given that Instagram is a huge platform (and Meta a notorious tracker), I thought you'd want to know.

### Proposed solution

This is more of a heads up than a specific feature request. The way to address this depends highly on the pattern in the parameters. It may not be worth overcomplicating the matching rules. If it's always 4 lowercase letters, though, it looks like you could use a regex to match them. If that's too broad, you can restrict it to certain paths (I've only seen these on `/reel/` urls).

### Additional information

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On aimanavo.com a first-party dark newsletter signup bottom sheet (`#reading-sheet`, activated by the site's own JS once the reader scrolls into the article) pops up over the lower mobile viewport and hides the article text — exactly the sheet in the reporter screenshot. Hiding that element restores the readable page with no layout damage, so the rule `aimanavo.com###reading-sheet` belongs in the AdGuard Popups filter's subscriptions section. ## Rule `aimanavo.com###reading-sheet` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's filter policy blocks rule generation only for the site's own advertising, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls, and unsupported anti-adblock walls. This report is none of those:⁠ it is a newsletter signup popup, which the AdGuard Popups filter is documented to cover ('Popups and forms for subscribing to news, promotions, and various events', KnowledgeBase filter-policy.md). The reporter's problem type (Annoyance) and the screenshot agree:⁠ a first-party newsletter bottom sheet covering article text, not an advertisement, a paywall or an anti-adblock wall. The fix fits an existing place in the repository (AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) and no maintainer rule restricts it. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/ba04be34179eee77898abfd71f7d1cbfa6875b31/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://www.mobiel.de/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.mobiel.de%2F) ### Comment > MoBiel is the public transport company of the city Bielefeld. The name is a play on words (Mobility for Bielefeld). The domain is blocked when typosquatting protection is enabled in AdguardDNS. This is not a new company or domain. I wonder how this got on the typosquatting protection list. This is a new issue. Does anyone check whether the affected domains are used deceptively? Even without knowing anything about the company, 30 seconds of investigation or even an automated check against domain registry information and Wikipedia would show that this a reputable, legitimate domain. > > This is not my first complaint the regarding typosquatting protection. Maybe it is better to turn it off, if no reasonable effort is put into assembly of this list. AI slop? ### Screenshots

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"199c502ffd64c1a948778fc9cb02d714116dc50b3a946846f2e1be63c1656697"} -->
The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Not reproduced — The reported anti-adblock interstitial ("Please allow ads on this site", "Failed to load website properly since html-load.com is blocked") did not appear in either an unfiltered Chromium session or a session with the AdGuard Browser Extension carrying the reporter's own settings (AdGuard Base + search-ads-unblocking filter):⁠ the forum homepage rendered normally in both, so there is nothing to build a rule against.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Instruction policy:⁠ "Any other anti-adblock wall:⁠ write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer." The report is not a German wall; no wall was observable at all in the live sessions, so no detector-script evidence could be gathered and the policy does not provide a rule to write. No repository rule closes this report:⁠ it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, and not a scam/malware case, so rule generation was permitted and evaluated on the evidence.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/44499374712

<sub>Automated analysis against filters at `eccc4c6`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.</sub>

1. **Fully stop the affected app.** Open Android Settings → Apps → select the affected app → **Force stop**.

3. **Clear the AdGuard filtering log.** Open AdGuard → **Statistics → Recent Activity** → tap the three-dot menu → **Clear recent activity**.

4. **Reproduce the issue.** Launch the affected app and perform the actions that cause the issue or make ads appear.

5. **Export the log.** In AdGuard, open **Statistics → Recent Activity** → tap the three-dot menu → **Export**.

7. **Submit the log for analysis (choose one of the following options):**

# Sorry. The website is infected by AdShield, Inc.

Unfortunately, It is complicated to resolve with a regular adblock rule because the website is being protected by service of Ad-Shield that is an anti-adblock company.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

@Alex-302 
In my environment, the anti-ad didn't appear, and I was able to resolve the issue with this rule:
`ygosu.com##.ygosu_banner[data-yg-banner-position]`
`ygosu.com###reply_list_layer > li:has(> .ygosu_banner[data-yg-banner-position="PC_REPLY"])`
`ygosu.com###board_article_list tr:has(> td.tit > a[href*="/board/real_article/ad/"])`
